output.brief: What is going on: the group's attrition is specific to Regulatory Investigations (37.5% against about 12% elsewhere) and it is concentrated on the Kestrel matter. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against one of the 13 others. All 11 Kestrel associates were supervised by Dorian Faulk, so the records cannot separate his supervision from the heavy review workload. Pay is the same across the group, and the billable-target change applied firm-wide while other groups stayed flat, so neither explains the pattern. Confidence: moderate that Kestrel is central; low on whether supervision or workload is the driver. Next: do not pay the group-wide retention payment or close the review. Commission the planned confidential interviews, designed to separate supervision from workload experiences, before choosing an intervention. Add supervisor and matter fields to attrition reporting. Revisit the Kestrel staffing plan once the interview results are in.
